summary: Reproducibility archive for the v14 revision (v1.2.0) of a multi-domain study of bone fragility in rheumatoid arthritis. The archive contains NHANES five-cycle analysis code and result tables, multi-dataset Mendelian randomization outputs, MHC specificity analyses, a post hoc DMARD-anchored sensitivity analysis (S31), an external T1D/AS MHC replication (S32 and Figure S10), the final manuscript and supplementary PDFs, and a data-source registry. Key findings: fracture history was associated with self-reported RA (OR 1.72, 1.27–2.32); the normal-BMD estimate was imprecise; OP diagnosis was diagnosis-dependent/ascertainment-sensitive; RA liability was associated with clinical OP and OP with pathological fracture, with borderline femur estimates; the MHC signal was shared for RA/T1D, whereas external AS instruments did not replicate. v1.2.0 (2026-10-19) corrects the pre-/post-harmonization SNP-count wording (Okada 45 selected, 37 analyzed for OP), describes the AS MHC estimate as nominally significant but not FDR-significant, and updates the word counts (abstract 239; main text 3,796). Raw third-party NHANES, FinnGen, and GWAS summary data are not redistributed; see data_sources/README_DATA_SOURCES.md.
title: Bone fragility in rheumatoid arthritis: phenotype-specific associations, a diagnosis-dependent osteoporosis signal, and a shared autoimmune MHC component

summary: This record contains the pair-level summaries, model-level matrices and analysis scripts for the manuscript Static Embeddings Are Poor Cross-Architecture Proxies: A Metric-Sensitive Reassessment . The archive covers 231 static pairs from 22 language models, a 153-pair multi-family static-to-contextual set from 18 models (Qwen 7, Gemma 4, SmolLM 4, Phi 3), and 91 layer-wise pairs from 14 models. The balanced set is analyzed with angular and Euclidean RDMs; the angular metric is primary. The archive includes the 22 x 22 Mantel, CKA, distance-correlation and Gromov-Wasserstein matrices, the 13 x 13 legacy proxy matrices, the 14 x 14 layer-wise Mantel and Procrustes matrices, the 153-pair extension table, the crossed random-effects inputs and outputs, and the scripts that reproduce them. Raw model weights, token-level distance matrices and cached hidden states are not included. The Procrustes values are shared-token subspace statistics, not full-width alignment. The static and multi-family sets are Qwen-heavy; the manuscript reports family-specific correlations and does not claim a uniform within-family effect. Code is released under GPL-3.0-or-later. Data and derived tables are released under CC BY 4.0. See README.md and PROVENANCE.md for file mapping, reproduction instructions and caveats.

summary: This repository provides the reproducible analysis materials accompanying the research article “Bitcoin and Sovereign Reserve Management: Portfolio Allocation, Model Sensitivity, and Downside Risk.” The study examines the sensitivity of Bitcoin allocations within a sovereign reserve-related portfolio framework, with particular emphasis on measurement consistency, model specification, allocation stability and downside risk. The empirical framework combines U.S. official reserve positions, Treasury gold holdings valued at market prices, and Bitcoin market-price observations. The principal estimation period covers April 2016 to July 2026, comprising 124 consecutive monthly changes. An extended historical sample beginning in January 2013 is used for sensitivity analysis. The analysis applies a Black–Litterman allocation framework with explicit budget constraints and alternative portfolio specifications. The reproducibility framework covers baseline portfolio estimation, alternative Bitcoin views and confidence levels, long-only allocation constraints, covariance sensitivity, rolling-window estimation, joint stationary bootstrap resampling and historical and hypothetical stress scenarios. summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code. Of 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,670 were used in another study and excluded from this analysis. Seventeen were excluded because their deposited assemblies did not meet the input criteria and raw-read download attempts were unsuccessful. The historical analyzable-input manifest therefore contained 42,591 records (40,094 public assemblies and 2,497 raw-derived inputs). Species adjudication excluded one record from each source, leaving 42,589 genomes: 40,093 public assemblies and 2,496 raw-derived genomes. Thirteen failed or unfinished raw-read attempts were retained through the public-assembly pathway and are not included in the 1,687 exclusions. Version 1.5.0 adds BioProject mapping for all 42,589 final genomes across 340 projects, descriptive project-level sensitivity analyses, updated record-disposition tables, and revised Figure 1 and Figure S1 materials. The locked primary cohort and primary statistical results remain unchanged. Exact-category sensitivity endpoints differ from the grouped primary endpoints; equal-project-weighted analyses and project bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Genome assemblies and raw reads were retrieved using a combination of scripts, download utilities, and manual downloads from repository webpages. Deposited assemblies were assessed first, with raw-read reconstruction attempted when a deposited assembly could not be retrieved or did not meet the input criteria. Exact historical read preprocessing commands could not be recovered. Adapter-trimming and quality-filtering parameters are outside this deposit’s reproducibility claim. Record-level logs documenting the 17 exclusions were unavailable. The deposit does not redistribute genome assemblies or raw sequencing reads. Retrieve sequence data from the original repositories using the supplied accession identifiers. Archived code supports the post-assembly cohort checks, primary statistical summaries, and BioProject sensitivity analyses. Jianhua Li and Jing Guo contributed equally. Jing Chen is the corresponding author (dongqingfei@126.com). Funding: Natural Science Foundation of Xiamen Municipality (3502Z202373092) and Xiamen Medical and Health Guidance Project (3502Z20254ZD1079).

summary: This paper presents a diagnostic theory that interprets a phenomenon observed in advanced economies—monetary easing and standard macroeconomic policies no longer generating sustained growth, even as they are accompanied by improvements in employment—not as a "failure of policy management" or a temporary demand shortfall, but as the structural depletion of investment outlets. As its core concepts, this paper introduces the structural frontier coefficient Φ, which represents the latent constraint determined by demographics, the institutional environment, and capital structure, and the critical threshold θ, at which policy effects undergo a qualitative shift. It further presents the "demand-constrained growth hypothesis" as the mechanism through which the structural frontier becomes constraining as the economy matures. The paper divides demand-side constraints into four types of goods—time-constrained goods, goods with strong ownership constraints, goods with weak ownership constraints and multiple ownership, and conduit goods—and organizes demand displacement and qualitative-improvement constraints as cross-cutting constraints superimposed on them. In an economy whose room for quantitative expansion has shrunk, the center of growth shifts to qualitative improvement; however, as the quality frontier is approached, the marginal cost of improvement rises while marginal utility and the scope for price pass-through may decline, so that technological progress may diverge from growth in sales and GDP. In the region Φ > θ, Solow-type growth theory and New Keynesian transmission may, by and large, function effectively, whereas in the region Φ ≤ θ, the spillover of monetary easing to real investment and sustained growth weakens, and easing tends instead to spill over into alternative channels such as asset prices, fund retention, and external capital movements. On the other hand, because the sensitivity of the employment channel to Φ is relatively lower than that of the growth channel, employment responses may remain relatively intact even in the region Φ ≤ θ. This asymmetry of the dual channels explains the simultaneous occurrence of employment improvement and growth stagnation. Under the definitional constraint that Φ is not back-calculated from outcome variables, this paper presents a two-layer diagnostic identification procedure. The structural state is diagnosed from the component-wise directions (structural signature) of the ordinal scale Φ̂, which is constructed without using outcome variables, and from the binding constraint; the policy transmission state is classified separately by the responses of the growth and alternative channels to identified monetary policy shocks (employment responses are checked as an auxiliary diagnosis); the two are then compared, with the estimate a of the realized investment ratio α, the cost-push coefficient κ, and other measures reported alongside as auxiliary findings. Furthermore, under the hypothesis that in mature, constrained regimes the elasticity of substitution declines and the dominant bottleneck determines the viability of investment, the paper positions the min approximation not as a predictive function but as a diagnostic limit. Companion empirical paper. This record also contains the companion empirical paper, "Does a Structural-Constraint Diagnosis Predict the Effectiveness of Monetary Easing? Exploratory Evidence from Within-Country Comparisons with Judgments Fixed before Matching" (Version 3, September 2026; English and Japanese PDFs, files named Watanabe_2026_*_Empirical_v3.pdf), which tests the central proposition of this paper.
title: General Theory of Structural Constraints: Investment Trap, Demand-Constrained Growth, and Regime Shifts in Monetary Policy Transmission

summary: Rationale. Implantation of permanent pacemakers in patients after repeat cardiac surgery can be significantly limited by cicatricial changes, recent cannulations, and obliteration of conventional venous accesses. An additional complication is the presence of congenital variants of systemic venous return, primarily persistent left superior vena cava (PSVC), which alters the geometry of endocardial electrode placement and increases the risk of technical complications. Case Description: This patient presented with a complex cardiac surgical history: aortic coarctation reconstruction in 2013, David I surgery in December 2025, and subsequent emergency hospitalization for decompensated chronic heart failure secondary to aortic valve avulsion and severe aortic regurgitation. On June 10, 2026, the patient underwent repeat aortic valve replacement with a Perceval L seamless biological valve prosthesis for life-saving reasons. In the early postoperative period, manifestations of sick sinus syndrome persisted, with transient second-degree sinoatrial block and pauses up to 3950 ms. Therefore, implantation of a dual-chamber, rate-adaptive pacemaker was planned for June 12, 2026. Intraoperatively, the standard right-sided approach was deemed unacceptable due to a fresh postoperative wound, severe tissue edema, and recent cannulation of the right subclavian artery. Upon conversion to the left subclavian approach, a stented septal vein (SVC) was detected with drainage through the dilated coronary sinus into the right atrium. Given preserved atrioventricular conduction, severe hypocoagulation, thrombocytopenia, and a high risk of coronary sinus injury, a decision was made to abandon the ventricular lead and perform single-chamber atrial pacing in AAIR mode. The lead with active fixation was successfully advanced through the splanchnic vein and the coronary sinus into the right atrium. Conclusion. This clinical observation demonstrates that in a patient with sick sinus syndrome and preserved atrioventricular conduction, AAIR mode can be a reasonable and technically safe option for permanent pacing when standard venous access is impossible and there is a high risk of ventricular lead placement through an anomalous venous collector.
title: FORCED INTRAOPERATIVE MODIFICATION OF PERMANENT CARDIAC PACING TACTICS THROUGH PERSISTENT LEFT SUPERIOR VENA CAVATA IN A HIGH-RISK PATIENT FOR CARDIAC SURGERY: A CASE REPORT

summary: Abstract and Prior-Art Disclosure  This manuscript serves as a formal public prior-art disclosure, conceptual research archive, and consolidated technical design dossier for the Metric Spacetime Manipulator 25 (MSM-25) architecture . As the direct successor to the MSM-24 revision, MSM-25 preserves the established topology, chronological provenance, authorship, and foundational physical mechanisms of the continuing research program, while introducing defining changes to the materials, output specifications, and operating mechanisms .  MSM-25 specifies a cryogenic superconducting device whose active core is a closed-loop chain of series-connected Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive Element (SNAIL) fluxonium cells, designated the SNAILonium . Adjacent galvanically connected SNAIL elements carry alternating loop chirality, with each element containing $n=3$ large Josephson junctions . Moving beyond its predecessor, MSM-25 admits a coplanar waveguide—with a ground plane conformal to the SNAIL contour and a widened gap near the junctions—alongside the superconducting flat wire ribbon . summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can self-evolve at test time by accumulating experience: retrieving relevant memories before acting and writing new lessons back afterwards. Yet most are single-level: trajectories, distilled workflows and reasoning items all land in one undifferentiated pool indexed by embedding similarity, with no typed abstraction hierarchy. They never forget or deduplicate, and are prone to negative transfer, where a superficially similar but directionally opposite experience is recalled and its concrete steps are copied verbatim, actively harming the agent. summary: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. summary: Agents are increasingly interacting with other agents that act for different principals (people or organizations on whose behalf they work), such as a buyer's personal agent negotiating with an enterprise's seller agent. In such agent-to-agent (A2A) scenarios, each agent has its own environment and holds information and authority that the other cannot see. From these traces, we derive $A^2$-Failures, a taxonomy of 20 A2A failure modes in four categories: (i) discovery and delegation, (ii) grounding and record consistency, (iii) verification, and (iv) conduct and fidelity. summary: NANOROBOTIC CARGO TRANSPORT AND MICROSCALE MANIPULATION INTEGRITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation DOI Fission Research Flagship 02 | Starli Active Nanosystems Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli | Research Atlas v1.0 (October 2026) How can a micro/nanorobotic carrier demonstrate that the object arriving at a designated target is the same intact cargo that was originally loaded, that it was completely and correctly released, and that the carrier or its residues have been accounted for? This English-language research atlas converts cargo-delivery and micromanipulation demonstrations into a falsifiable end-to-end mission-integrity problem. The research develops a five-layer architecture for source identity and material tolerance, microscale contact mechanics, independently observable mission-state transitions, adversarial fault injection, and blind cross-platform requalification. Thirty mathematically distinct derivation stations connect probabilistic joint-task qualification to chemical mass balance, optical-label dissociation, surface adsorption, force-dependent detachment, microcontact mechanics, drag, kinetic release, spatial uncertainty, carryover contamination, whole-facility energy accounting, missing-fate bounds and hard safety vetoes. Eighty-two chapters each have a dedicated core-equation opening and five separate research sections. Two hundred Research Gates propose independent comparisons, physical perturbations, competing explanations, measurable failure criteria and reproducibility artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate systems that future investigators are invited to overturn, repair or rebuild. A machine-readable research atlas and formula-gate-DOI index enable AI-assisted comparison and future research reuse. The central endpoint is a correlated joint event: correct cargo identity and integrity, correct target, independently confirmed release, and verified carrier retrieval or authorized terminal disposition. The manuscript insists on counting every initiated mission rather than multiplying attractive substep success rates. It also distinguishes visible fluorescence from chemically intact cargo, externally actuated manipulation from on-board autonomy, and destination arrival from complete task closure. Strong benchmarks include optical tweezers, established magnetic-bead handling, microfluidic conveyance and conventional microgrippers under matched task difficulty, time and whole-facility energy use. Research status: This is a hypothesis-generating, nonclinical experimental-design atlas; it reports no newly conducted cargo experiments, clinical performance or proven integrated device. Foundational and recent DOI-identified publications provide engineering context but do not validate its new claims. The 200 Gates are open problems, not accomplished results. summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23431625 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes The introduction clearly explains the research objectives. It states that the study aims to replicate the quantitative analysis of Krause, Krause, and Bränfors (2018), assess the reproducibility of their findings, and examine potential limitations concerning statistical power and model specification. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate The replication approach is suitable for the research, as the authors reproduce the original Cox proportional hazards models and robustness tests. However, the methodological assessment has some gaps. In particular, the power analysis reports values of 0.44 and 0.99 without providing the formula, software procedure, or sufficient calculation details to allow readers to reproduce the estimates. The choice of 42 events in Table 6 also needs clarification, given that Table 5 reports 54 events overall. Additionally, the differences between the original and reproduced sample sizes remain unexplained. These issues weaken the transparency and reproducibility of the analysis. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported The main conclusion is that the original findings can be reproduced, which is supported by the reported results. The authors also reasonably identify the small number of female-signatory agreements and the limitations of drawing causal conclusions from the observed association. However, the claim that the analysis has low statistical power relies on a calculation for which the formula and detailed procedure are not provided (Table 6). The differences between the original and reproduced sample sizes also remain unexplained. These limitations make some aspects of the interpretation less conclusive than they could be. Are the data presentations, including visualizations, well-suited to represent the data? Somewhat appropriate and clear The survival analysis and regression tables are suitable for presenting the findings. However, some numerical inconsistencies in the descriptive statistics and differences in sample sizes across the original and reproduced models need clarification to ensure the results are presented accurately. For instance, Table 3 presents: three major statistical flaws: 1: Conflict Intensity row, where Female Signatories = 1: has SD of 1.2 while the Max is 0.45, which is statistically incorrect. Similarly, (2) Democracy row where Female Signatories = 1, has Mean 0.92 < Min 1. And lastly, on page 5, UN peacekeeping is written as a binary number, however, in Table 3, the binary UN Peacekeeping has Max > 1. All these minor inconsistencies require clarification. How clearly do the authors discuss, explain, and interpret their findings and potential next steps for the research? Very clearly The authors explain their findings, acknowledge the limitations of the small number of agreements with female signatories, and discuss the implications for causal interpretation. They also identify the need for further research, although the power analysis and differences in sample sizes could be explained more transparently. Is the preprint likely to advance academic knowledge? Somewhat likely If the author clarified the sample-size discrepancies and documented the power analysis more transparently, then it would substantially contribute to the reproducibility of an influential finding, as it already highlights the reproducibility of the findings and highlights the limitations in statistical power and causal interpretation. summary: This paper studies parameter families of finite exponential sums in which two tie endpoints of a near-maximum level set approach at the critical rate δ_r ≍ qr^{-1/2}. The endpoint separation, half-bowl width, and competitor-kernel decay length then coincide. The cluster trio is rigid: its three exponents are determined by the level and endpoint positions, while coefficient ratios and other competitors require separate control. In a realized family, six rescaled kernels carry the interaction through one microscopic phase. Under explicit kernel-convergence hypotheses, the second-order term has a joint limit given by the excess sublevel length of a limiting profile, decomposed into a separated-endpoint sum and an interaction term. For an explicit four-term family, the hypotheses are verified with uniform explicit constants for every admissible phase lock. Two families have identical spectra and corresponding coefficient moduli at every radius but different critical limits. Along an unlocked calibration, phase dependence yields non-existence of the critical limit for specified parameters; certified intervals quantify the gap, and failure persists on an open parameter set. For a positive zero-lock family, upper and lower bounds describe the excluded shared arc. Full exclusion never occurs, and nonempty exclusion requires an additional parameter condition. The formal endpoint-anchored cap cannot be realized by a family satisfying the cluster hypotheses. High-precision numerical measurements on actual exponential sums compare with the profiles and exhibit phase dependence.
title: Critical-Scale Clustering and the Breakdown of Universality for Near-Maximum Phase Measures of Exponential Sums

summary: We consider the three-dimensional Prandtl boundary layer equations near a smooth structured solution (u_s, K u_s) with ∂z K ≡ 0. Under a monotone-or-degenerate profile assumption on u_s(·), we prove local well-posedness, continuous dependence, and a priori estimates in the critical Sobolev space X^s = H^s_γ(r) × H^s_γ(q) × H^s_γ(∇{x,y} q), where r = u − u_s and q = v − K u. Our proof does not assume smallness of the data, monotonicity of ∂_z u_s, or Gevrey regularity. We also establish a nonlinear norm-inflation result showing that the raw H^s topology on q alone is insufficient, and we identify the minimal tangential derivative of q required. summary: We investigate the rigidity of smooth stationary solutions to the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in ℝⁿ with singularities along a linear subspace Σ ≅ ℝᵏ. Assuming the scale-invariant transverse bound ‖u(x)‖ ≤ C‖x′‖⁻¹, where x′ ∈ ℝᵐ represents the transverse coordinates and m = n − k is the codimension of the singularity, we prove that u ≡ 0 provided m ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ k < m. This result generalizes the recent theorem of Gui, Liu, Wang, and Xie (2026), which corresponds to the case k = 1 and n ≥ 5. Our proof relies on a quantitative local regularity theorem showing that the transverse bound implies the removability of the singularity along Σ. The argument combines weak extension across the subspace, approximate Green functions for the adjoint drift operator, a one-sided bound for the total head pressure, and a localized Frehse–Růžička weighted estimate followed by a finite Stokes–Morrey bootstrap. Furthermore, we establish the sharpness of the codimension threshold m ≥ 4 by constructing non-trivial counterexamples for m = 1, m = 2, and m = 3 via trivial extensions of Jeffery–Hamel and Landau solutions, together with a new explicit family of non-trivial solutions in the borderline case m = 1. Finally, we discuss the technical obstruction preventing the immediate removal of the condition k < m and propose a conditional rigidity result under additional integrability assumptions.
title: RIGIDITY OF STATIONARY NAVIER–STOKES SOLUTIONS WITH TRANSVERSE BOUNDS NEAR HIGHER-CODIMENSIONAL SINGULAR SUBSPACES

summary: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.

summary: Background. Antireflux fundoplication failure — recurrent reflux, dysphagia, gas-bloat syndrome, secondary to a herniated, slipped, too-tight, disrupted, or twisted valve — remains common, and its endoscopic diagnosis lacks a common, standardized reporting language. Aim. To narratively review existing endoscopic instruments for postoperative antireflux valve assessment, the evidence on their interobserver reliability, and to position an original instrument — the Endoscopic Fundoplication Score (SEF) — within this landscape. Methods. Narrative review, with a targeted search in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar (last search: 24 September 2026) using the terms “fundoplication,” “endoscopic grading,” “gastroesophageal valve,” “Hill classification,” “antireflux surgery outcome,” “interobserver reliability,” “wrap integrity,” and “hiatal hernia recurrence,” covering literature published between 1996 and 2026 in English or with an English abstract, supplemented by reference-list screening of identified articles. Results. Three major endoscopic instruments were identified — the Hill classification (1996), the Jobe system (2004), and the American Foregut Society (AFS) nomenclature (2025) — alongside a descriptive, non-scored taxonomy of failure types (herniated, slipped, tight, disrupted, twisted). The interobserver reliability studies [1,2] identified in this review for the postoperative setting report low agreement, and a retrospective comparison of endoscopy reports [3] documented major discrepancies between external endoscopists and operating surgeons. The AFS classification of esophagogastric junction integrity achieved substantial agreement on static images (κ=0.65) but only fair agreement under dynamic conditions (κ=0.371), and the postoperative AFS nomenclature has not yet been tested for interobserver reliability. The SEF score, an 11-item composite instrument (0–16 points) applied to a cohort of 178 patients, correlated in preliminary single-centre data with the Hill classification, Los Angeles (LA) esophagitis grade, and the Visick patient-satisfaction score (own data, manuscript submitted for publication), offering a numeric, quantifiable alternative to existing categorical systems. The SEF threshold of ≤10 points, defined in the same cohort, is exploratory. Conclusions. The field of postoperative endoscopic antireflux valve assessment remains fragmented, without an interobserver-reliable consensus standard. The SEF score partially addresses this gap through a numeric structure, with experience-based weights and an exploratory threshold, but requires formal interobserver reliability testing and multicenter validation against the surgical gold standard.
title: ENDOSCOPIC EVALUATION OF THE ANTIREFLUX VALVE AFTER FUNDOPLICATION: SYNTHESIS OF THE EVIDENCE AND PROPOSAL OF A FUNCTIONAL ENDOSCOPIC SCORE

summary: NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? A sound, a face, a tightness in the chest. Before you have chosen anything, a voice — yours, apparently — has already named it, judged it, and filed it under a chapter called me. You do not notice the filing. You notice the file. And so you spend your days inside a commentary about a world you have not, strictly speaking, met. This is not a moral failure. It is a timing error. Awareness is not a mood you work up and not a belief you adopt. It is what is already underway before the sentence starts. The breath you are taking does not consult your biography. The light on the wall does not ask what you meant to become. For a fraction of a second there is contact without a commentator. Then the commentator returns, a little late, a little proud, and explains what just occurred as if the explanation were the event. People talk about waking up as if it were a prize for the patient and the pure. It is closer to catching a clerical mistake. You have been treating the report as the room. The report is useful. Watch the exact moment a thought claims you. There is a sensation, then a grab. The grab feels like identity. It is older than that, and thinner. It is a habit of ownership so practiced it forgot it was optional. You do not have to defeat it. You only have to notice that noticing is already happening, and that the one who seems to be doing the noticing cannot be found as an object inside what is noticed. Sit with that past the point of comfort. Comfort is how the narration gets rehired. If the “you” who plans, defends, remembers, and suffers is a pattern appearing in awareness, then who has been afraid all this time? Not a cosmic answer. A local one. Look. Fear is weather. The sky it crosses was not manufactured by the storm. Nothing theatrical follows from this. You will still want things. You will still lose them. You will still answer the message and miss the person. The only change is a small, stubborn order of operations: experience first, story second. And the recognition, quiet enough to miss if you perform it, that you were never inside the story. You were the place it was being told. That place does not improve. It does not arrive. It does not need you to become someone else in order to be what it already is. The only work, if it can even be called work, is to stop leaving a half-second early — to remain, once, with what is here before you agree with your own explanation of it. Stay. We argue that effective leadership in this new era requires designing trust-enabling infrastructures, ensuring human-centric governance of management algorithms, and fostering portable skill development for a transient workforce. This paper introduces novel theoretical perspectives, including temporal leadership dynamics, polycontextual leadership challenges, and the concept of reverse leadership flows from workers to platforms. By presenting a comprehensive model supported by data visualizations and identifying avenues for empirical validation, this research offers a forward-looking agenda for both scholars and practitioners navigating the complexities of leadership in the 21st-century workforce.

summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

summary: Popper’s (1983, 2002) philosophy of science has enjoyed something of a renaissance in the wake of the replication crisis, offering a philosophical basis for the ensuing science reform movement. However, adherence to Popper’s approach may also be at least partly responsible for the sense of “crisis” that has developed following multiple unexpected replication failures. In this article, I contrast Popper’s approach with that of Lakatos (1978) as well as with a related but problematic approach called naïve methodological falsificationism (NMF; Lakatos, 1978). The Popperian approach is powerful because it is based on logical refutations, but its theories are noncausal and, therefore, potentially lacking in scientific value. In contrast, the Lakatosian approach considers causal theories, but it concedes that these theories are not logically refutable. Finally, NMF represents a hybrid approach that subjects Lakatosian causal theories to Popperian logical refutations. However, its tactic of temporarily accepting a ceteris paribus clause during theory testing may be viewed as scientifically inappropriate, epistemically inconsistent, and “completely redundant” (Lakatos, 1978, p. 40). I conclude that the replication “crisis” makes the most sense in the context of the Popperian and NMF approaches because it is only in these two approaches that the failure to replicate a previously corroborated theory represents a logical refutation of that theory. In contrast, such replication failures are less problematic in the Lakatosian approach because they do not logically refute theories. Indeed, in the Lakatosian approach, replication failures can be temporarily ignored or used to motivate theory development.
title: The replication crisis is less of a "crisis" in Lakatos' philosophy of science than it is in Popper's.

summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.

summary: This dataset tests whether public density-functional-theory (DFT) databases can guide composition selection for metastable magnet phases. It compares energy above the convex hull and computed Fe moments from Materials Project, AFLOW, JARVIS-DFT, NOMAD (Alexandria PBE calculations), OQMD and GNoME (628 entries, snapshot 2026-10-13) with 38 published observations of phases formed in Sm–Fe and Sm–Fe–M alloys (M = Co, Ti, V, Zr, Nb, Cu, Si, Ga, Al, Mo; none found for Cr, Mn, Hf) after rapid solidification or mechanical milling, 30 of which are scored. Because no database contains the disordered TbCu7 structure, a stability proxy is built from each database's ordered parents (CaCu5, 2:17, 3:29, ThMn12); the proxy and per-family best entries are given in stability_proxy_table.csv . Main finding: Materials Project, OQMD and Alexandria place no Sm–Fe compound on the convex hull, so their energies for equilibrium Sm2Fe17, metastable TbCu7 SmFe9 and SmFe12 (not formed by melt spinning) differ by less than 5 meV/atom. JARVIS-DFT ranks them correctly but places TbCu7 SmFe9 at 89 meV/atom. AFLOW and GNoME contain no comparable entries. The package contains raw database snapshots with provenance (SHA-256), the curated observation table with DOIs, numbered pipeline scripts (Python), a QA report, four figures and documentation (codebook, limitations, verification checklist). Code: MIT. Data and documents: CC BY 4.0. AI assistance: data retrieval scripts, curation drafting and analysis code were prepared with an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic); the author verified the numbers and decisions before release.
title: TbCu7 Stability Screen: validation of public DFT databases against observed metastable phases in Sm–Fe–M alloys (stability proxy table)

summary: mm-ADL-Home is a cross-environment millimeter-wave radar point-cloud dataset for human activity recognition in furnished residential environments. The dataset was collected in four indoor environments comprising three simulated bachelor-unit layouts and one real bachelor unit, using the same activity taxonomy and radar configuration as the mm-ADL dataset (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22405011).  Each participant–environment recording is preserved as a continuous point-cloud stream and includes: (1) point_cloud.csv , containing radar point-cloud observations; (2) frame_labels.csv , containing frame-level activity annotations; (3) timestamps.csv , providing the temporal correspondence between radar and annotation frames; and (4) location_annotations.csv , containing the intervals used to register the radar sensor and landmark furniture in the radar coordinate system. The activity taxonomy covers locomotion, sitting and lying transitions, stationary sitting and lying, simulated falls, and floor-to-standing recovery. Location annotations identify sittable furniture, lieable furniture, kitchen locations, entry locations, and the radar sensor origin. These annotations support the reconstruction of room-level spatial context and furniture landmarks on the horizontal radar coordinate plane. The dataset contains complete recordings without a prescribed windowing or segmentation scheme, allowing users to implement their own preprocessing, temporal segmentation, domain adaptation, and evaluation protocols. Synchronized RGB recordings used during annotation are not included in the public release. Participant identifiers are pseudonymous.
title: mm-ADL-Home: A Cross-Environment Millimeter-Wave Radar Point-Cloud Dataset for Activities of Daily Living in Furnished Homes

summary: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 allows a child aged sixteen or seventeen who is alleged to have committed a heinous offence to be tried as an adult after a "preliminary assessment" by the Juvenile Justice Board. This paper argues that the transfer mechanism is less a principled answer to serious adolescent offending than a legislative compromise whose costs fall on the procedural guarantees the Act otherwise extends to children. It reads section 15 against the Supreme Court's decisions in Shilpa Mittal and Barun Chandra Thakur, the age-determination case law, and the developmental research on adolescent culpability, and it engages the retributive and victim-centred case for transfer on its own terms. Accountability and rehabilitation, the paper contends, are not two poles to be traded off at a single age threshold. Both depend on institutional capacity that the system has never been resourced to supply: functioning Boards, trained probation staff, individual care plans that are actually followed, and aftercare that reaches young people beyond eighteen. Reform should narrow and proceduralise transfer, introduce statutory diversion, decouple offence classification from the general penal code, and treat implementation failure as a rights violation rather than an administrative shortfall.
title: Reforming Juvenile Justice in India: Balancing Child Rights, Accountability, and Rehabilitation

summary: Lecture 1 formulated the recommendation problem in abstract terms: a set of users U , a set of items I , and a preference function r(u,i) that must be estimated for the pairs that have not been observed. Every algorithm studied in this course, however, operates on concrete data rather than on abstractions. The quality of a recommender system is therefore bounded by the quality, the structure, and the representation of the data from which it learns. In practice, improving the data frequently brings larger gains than changing the algorithm. A sophisticated model trained on noisy, biased, or poorly prepared data produces poor recommendations, a principle often summarized as garbage in, garbage out . This lecture therefore addresses three questions: è Which data does a recommender system collect, and what do these data really mean? è How can these data be organized and represented so that algorithms can process them? è How must the data be prepared and partitioned before a model is built and assessed? After studying this lecture, the reader should be able to: · Identify the sources and categories of data used in a recommender system; · Characterize explicit and implicit feedback, including their strengths and weaknesses; · Construct a user–item matrix and interpret its sparsity; · Represent users and items as vectors built from interactions and descriptive features; · Apply the main preprocessing operations to ratings and implicit signals; · Split a dataset correctly and avoid information leakage. The path followed by the data throughout this lecture is: Data sources → Feedback signals → User–item matrix → Vector representations → Preprocessing → Data splitting
title: Lecture Notes on Recommender Systems

summary: Section 166(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires directors to act with 'due and reasonable care, skill and diligence' and to exercise 'independent judgment'. The provision was drafted for human decision-makers and is silent on what that duty demands when a board relies on an algorithmic system whose reasoning it cannot inspect. This article argues that the gap is practical, not theoretical. Indian courts have not fixed a consistent standard of care, the protections available to directors under sections 463 and 149(12) operate only after a dispute arises, and the regulatory material now addressing AI in Indian finance, from SEBI's 2025 consultation paper to the RBI's FREE-AI report and 2026 draft model-risk guidance and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, binds entities rather than defining the individual director's duty of care. Drawing on Delaware's process-based oversight cases and on the distinction between substance and process in corporate governance scholarship, the article proposes a five-part Board AI Oversight Standard (identify, understand, challenge, monitor and document). It recommends two routes to give the Standard legal force: an amendment to Regulation 21 and Schedule II of the SEBI Listing Regulations, and a rebuttable presumption of due care under section 166(3) for boards that follow it. The proposal gives firms an ex ante and auditable benchmark for defending board decisions, and gives courts a workable test.
title: Who Is Minding the Algorithm? Section 166(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 and a Process Standard for AI-Assisted Board Decisions

summary: PHOTONIC CRYSTAL MICROROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT FLAGSHIP 12/30 | STARLI INSTITUTE XXIV | GROUP B This prospective research monograph examines whether bandgap engineering and localized photonic crystal modes can enable physically predictable, reversible optical manipulation of microscopic agents when actual device geometry, absorption, hydrodynamic flow, surface adhesion, thermal limits, and task cost are fully considered. The three core couplings are photonic bands, microstructure response, and controllable motion. The book separates optical modes from attributable electromagnetic momentum transfer, and further separates externally steered particles or cells from autonomous microrobots. Its falsifiable research design compares two lattice-defect geometries, source-frequency interventions, local thermal controls, optimized free-space optical tweezers, non-periodic waveguide traps, and blinded second-chip replication. High Q or strong local field alone is not accepted as evidence of useful lower-power microrobotic performance. The manuscript contains 778 pages, approximately 119,409 English words in chapter openings and substantive chapter-body pages, 30 mathematical derivation signposts with mapped chapters and research questions, 82 research chapters, 410 individually paginated scientific study units, 200 detailed Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. An external DOI evidence ledger clarifies which physical contexts are supported by published work; four existing STARLI monographs supply intellectual genealogy, not experimental corroboration. An Excel research atlas offers equation-chapter-Gate-DOI navigation. A research Gate poses a future experiment, not a completed trial. Each door may be falsified, reinterpreted, or developed into a more testable hypothesis. The project prioritizes measurable physical mechanism, credible classical comparators, complete power and loss accounting, reproducible material controls, and release/recovery of agents. Negative outcomes are intentionally preserved as routes for later human and AI research successors.

summary: Research compendium for the article "Climate warming is projected to reduce and redistribute Aedes albopictus abundance, away from Po Valley hotspots towards Alpine margins" (M. C. Darılmaz, Science of the Total Environment; manuscript STOTEN-D-26-01129R1). The study predicts weekly ovitrap egg counts of the Asian tiger mosquito at 149 monitoring stations in Italy, Albania, Switzerland and France (VectAbundance, 2010–2022). The framework has four layers: a mechanistic life-history model (dynamAedes 2.2.9); gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) and random forests with climate, remote-sensing, land-use, demographic and population-genetic predictors; an ablation of the population-genetic layer; and projections under 48 CMIP6 combinations (four General Circulation Models, three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways, four periods to 2100). The archive contains: - 48 Python, 8 R and 1 Google Earth Engine scripts, with PIPELINE.md giving the order in which they run; - the processed station-level data and the final modelling tables (42,118 station–week records), with the station-to-fold assignment used by every cross-validated analysis; - the trained XGBoost and Random Forest models with their cross-validation predictions, feature importance and SHAP values; - the outputs of the ablation and sensitivity analyses: mechanistic and genetic ablations, genetic structure versus geographic position, fold-count sensitivity, fold-level inference, feature correlation and VIF, spatio-temporal and leave-one-year-out cross-validation, remote-sensing gap-filling, baseline period, calibration and validation detail, treatment of the year predictor, inputs that carry the projected change, and the fill of weeks without mechanistic output; - the inputs and outputs of the 48-scenario projection, per climate model, as ensemble and at station level. Main results reproduced by the archive: cross-validated R² of the full model 0.534 ± 0.093 (XGBoost; pooled 0.539) and 0.544 ± 0.081 (Random Forest). Projected change in mean active-season abundance over the 12 SSP–period combinations: −4 to −27 % at Hot lowland stations (−6 to −44 % in the Po Valley) and +10 to +106 % at Cool upland and Alpine margin stations. Raw inputs that are publicly available from their primary archives (ERA5-Land, WorldClim 2.1 and its CMIP6 projections, satellite imagery, GHS-POP, the population-genetic source data and GenBank sequences) are not redistributed; README.md lists the sources and how the scripts locate them. Licence: CC BY 4.0.
title: Climate warming is projected to reduce and redistribute Aedes albopictus abundance, away from Po Valley hotspots towards Alpine margins

summary: Notes cover the changes since 0.5.0. pip install metabeta==0.6.0 Tutorials Three notebooks in demos/ replace intro.ipynb and priors.ipynb . Each runs on a CPU runtime in Colab. 01-quickstart : lme4's sleepstudy end to end, next to lme4's estimates. 02-families : Bernoulli ( cbpp ) and Poisson ( Salamanders ) fits, posterior predictive checks, and random-walk moves next to a NUTS reference. 03-priors : prior specification, prior sensitivity in one call, and model comparison by Bayes factors. New reports posteriorDraws(result) : posterior draws of the global parameters on the data's scale, as a DataFrame named as in posteriorSummary (#31). groupDraws(result) : each group's coefficients per draw, the fixed effect plus the group's deviation (#33). posteriorPredictive(result) : the observed responses and one replicate per posterior draw, in the data's units (#33). bayesFactor(result, reference) : the Bayes factor of one model over another, per prior, with its Kass–Raftery grade; both results come from sample(evidence=True) (#33). sample n_samples defaults to 1,000 draws (#19). seed= makes a call reproducible and leaves the caller's random stream untouched (#32). posteriorPredictive and plotPPD take seed= too (#26, #33). Every summary ends with a fit metric: R² (Gaussian), AUC (Bernoulli) or deviance (Poisson) (#29). loo=True adds PSIS-LOO to the summary; it replaces diagnostics=True (#29). random_walk=True runs silently and warns only below an IMH effective sample size (ESS) of 10 (#29). Warnings state the failure, its consequence and numbered remedies, and point at the user's call (#18, #29). The first call after loading costs about as much as a warm one; warmup() runs that pass explicitly (#19). Formulas, scales and names Formulas follow lme4: y ~ 1 + (1 | g) fits an intercept-only model, preprocessing reads only the columns the formula names, and column names keep their case (#15). The order of fixed terms no longer changes the fit; names are mapped back in every output (#16). Summaries default to x_scale='original' . Random-effect SDs, correlations and per-group effects are on the data's scale like the fixed effects, and so are the prior lines (#17). rfxSummary labels each group correctly (#17). Api.from_pretrained('gaussian') is an alias of 'normal' , in any case (#30). Reports pick a dataset row by prior_id , a prior's name or its index (#32). summary: This article proposes a theoretical framework for transporting large physical masses at the speed of light C by analyzing the behavior of photons through advanced single-photon imaging techniques. By examining the temporal and spatial distribution of photons captured via Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) cameras, we establish a correlation between the visual reconstruction of an object and its potential physical translation across space-time. We argue that light possesses an inherent volumetric, cell-like structure capable of carrying mass, provided an engineering mechanism can replicate its fundamental properties: diffraction, momentum, and precise synchronization.
tags: proof of possible travel at light speed
title: Single-photon imaging is evidence of the possibility of mass traveling at the speed of light.

summary: We establish almost infinite log-monotonicity of the Bell numbers, settling a conjecture of Chen, Guo and Wang (2013). The result extends to the Touchard sequence Tn(λ) = Pk S(n, k)λk for every fixed λ > 0. For each integer m ≥ 2, (−1)m∆m log Tn(λ) ∼ (m − 2)!n1−m , uniformly for λ in compact subsets of (0, ∞). We obtain two further terms in inverse powers of W(n/λ) through an arbitrary-order saddle-point expansion and direct estimates for finite differences.
title: Almost infinite log-monotonicity of Bell and Touchard sequences

summary: This record holds the preregistration, code, outputs, process logs and session transcripts of a study that is also a meta-experiment on research produced almost entirely by an AI agent (Claude, model claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic, run in Claude Code) under the direction of one researcher. The substantive study asks a deliberately implausible question: is living with a cat associated with untreated dental decay among US adults? It uses public data from NHANES 2005–2006 with survey-weighted modified Poisson regression, prespecified confounders, sensitivity analyses and equivalence testing. The preregistered primary result was inconclusive (prevalence ratio 1.12, 95% CI 0.93 to 1.36). The meta-experiment measures what producing the study took: time, human interventions, agent errors and the share of code and text written by the agent. The accompanying preprint, "Do cats rot your teeth? A by-the-book paper written by an AI agent, and what it means for scientific communication", shows how four of the 45 preregistered estimates could support a positive paper without breaking the registration, and argues that verification, not writing, is now the bottleneck of scientific communication. Version 1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23435708) is the frozen preregistration, deposited before any exposure–outcome association was computed and later registered on OSF (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/RVH7J). Its files remain available in version 1. summary: We develop a counterfactual semantics based on reopening partial information states. Evaluation first removes enough stated content to leave the antecedent’s attributes unresolved, retaining what the chosen scope protects, then asserts the antecedent and considers the surviving consistent refinements. Would and might quantify over the admissible alternatives; a weighted extension supplies graded evaluations. The principal result concerns finite models with fully supported residues. When a conjunctive antecedent reopens each constituent attribute, adding a supported conjunct can remove the grounds of another conclusion. A four-attribute countermodel therefore violates Cautious Monotony, excluding any smooth preferential representation that preserves the evaluable verdicts. We also establish a sufficient nesting condition for Cut and exhibit its failure without that condition. The conjunctive reopening rule is an explicit interpretive commitment; its suitability for ordinary-language counterfactuals remains an empirical question. The account uses declared dependencies, scope restrictions, and priorities, while the quantitative extension assumes a weight kernel. Comparisons with belief revision, premise semantics, update semantics, and causal intervention identify the consequences of reopening an attribute rather than merely making its proposed value consistent with retained information.
title: Counterfactual Evaluation by Reopening Information States

summary: Replication package for the article Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities . It contains the code, the estimation data and the documentation needed to reproduce every table, figure and number reported in the article and its online appendix. Study The article links administrative payroll records of tenure-line faculty at 93 U.S. public universities (fiscal years 2004–2026) to their publication records in OpenAlex. For each department it estimates a department-specific pay equation and measures the pay dispersion that the department’s formal ladder (rank, contract basis, seniority) does not explain. This residualized Gini is related to five dimensions of members’ research: productivity, citations, novelty, conventionality and disruption. The analytic sample has 124,056 department-person records, covering 105,050 faculty members in 4,839 departments. Contents README.md : overview, layout, coding of identifiers, environment. HANDOFF_FOR_AI_AGENTS.md : the pipeline end to end (inputs, outputs, run order, checkpoints), with a map from each table, figure and number of the paper to the script and file that produce it. Written for an AI agent or a human reader.  DATA_DICTIONARY.md : every column of every data file in 3_analysis/ . 1_data_collection/ : code that acquired and parsed the public salary disclosures, plus the department backfill, Wayback supplement (code only). 2_data_cleaning_and_linking/ : code that assembled the salary panel, standardized names, ranks and departments, linked faculty to OpenAlex authors, and computed the work-level measures (code only). 3_analysis/ : the pseudonymised estimation frames and the analysis code (first stage, panel and matching, tables, figures, appendix analyses), with the shipped outputs. run_all.sh and notebooks_step_by_step/ : the full analysis as one shell script, and the same pipeline as one Jupyter notebook per script in run order (outputs saved). Reproducing the results Install the pinned environment (Python 3.12.7 and the exact versions in requirements.txt , x86-64 Linux), then run run_all.sh or the notebooks in order. The analysis in 3_analysis/ runs end to end from the shipped frames and needs no API key; a full run takes about 15 minutes on a multi-core machine (the first-stage bootstrap runs 12 parallel processes of about 3.5 GB each; set S19_WORKERS lower on a smaller machine). run_all.sh records each step in run_status.tsv and writes a SHA-256 manifest of the outputs ( run_manifest.tsv ). Folders 1 and 2 document how the data were produced; they require the raw source caches, an OpenAlex snapshot and SciSciNet, and are not re-runnable from this package. Data and privacy The salary records are public disclosures, but they name individuals. In this replication package, universities, departments and people are replaced by codes (for example  AZ University A , AZ University A Employee 00042 ). The mapping is held by the author and is not distributed. The frames retain exact salary, fiscal year, rank, career age, state and inferred gender and race, so the data are pseudonymised. Please do not attempt to re-identify individuals. License CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Please cite the article when using this package.
title: Replication package for "Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities"

summary: Space Semiconductor Fabrication and Starship Nanofoundries at the Limit English Description and Research Position This research monograph asks which semiconductor unit processes could achieve a defensible mission advantage in microgravity, vacuum, radiation, remote-operation, and closed-resource environments. It does not assume that a complete advanced fab can operate in space. Instead, it compares crystal growth, deposition, etching, lithography, metrology, bonding, packaging, repair, and recycling against ground manufacture plus transport, launched spares, on-orbit packaging, and local repair. Every claimed advantage must survive matched controls, full functional qualification, and explicit mass, energy, heat, crew, contamination, maintenance, waste, and return ledgers. The volume contains 82 chapters with five research sections per chapter, 30 linked formula derivations, 200 detailed Research Gates, DOI-anchored references, and a formula-chapter-experiment-Gate crosswalk. Its central contribution is a mission-scale evidence architecture that connects process physics to contained workcells, independent metrology, safe autonomy, repair, return, circular resources, cross-platform reproduction, and successor reconstruction. Safety and irreversible environmental harm operate as hard vetoes rather than compensable score components. The literature base includes peer-reviewed DOI sources on microgravity semiconductor growth, in-space manufacturing, additive nanomanufacturing, atomic-layer processing, radiation effects, lunar resource extraction, digital twins, autonomous laboratories, and reproducible science. Recent orbital results are treated as early evidence for specific mechanisms, not as confirmation of a complete space foundry. Core research question Under what physical and mission conditions can a semiconductor unit process performed in space outperform ground manufacture plus transport or a narrower in-space alternative while preserving safety, resource closure, qualification, and independent reconstruction? Research architecture • Space-specific process advantage and strongest comparator • Environmental physics and bounded process window • Closed mass energy heat contamination and evidence ledgers • Autonomy safeing repair return and independent qualification • Cross-platform reproduction successor rebuild and retirement Recommended citation note This is an exploratory research architecture. Candidate equations are measurement and mission-decision instruments, not universal laws. Empirical use requires process-specific units, preregistration, matched controls, aerospace and semiconductor expertise, independent qualification, and cross-platform replication.

summary: Living Concept Embodiment and Real World Action Translation at the Limit English Description and Research Position This research monograph investigates how an abstract concept becomes an observable, measurable, and revisable pattern of action. It follows the full translation chain from a sourced proposition to operational rules, interfaces, institutional conduct, distributed outcomes, protected dissent, correction, rollback, and successor reconstruction. The book does not treat concepts as physical organisms or assume that institutional adoption proves success. Embodiment is framed as a falsifiable socio-technical claim: independent reviewers should be able to identify the mechanism, distinguish it from rhetoric and attention effects, observe who benefits and who bears hidden costs, and determine when a branch must be revised or stopped. Rights and irreversible-harm boundaries operate as hard vetoes rather than compensable score components. summary: This computational package accompanies the Neuro-Symbolic MAPE-K governance testbed for agentic retrieval-augmented generation at the edge. It provides Python source, experimental inputs, measured outputs, provenance manifests, analysis tables, figures and readable evidence reports for two related campaigns: the October 2026 MAPE-K controller campaign and the separate 18 October 2026 dense-retriever control campaign. The retriever control records 3,744 retrieval trials and 640 clean-validation query evaluations across sparse, pretrained dense and clean-fitted dense retrievers. It performs no new generator or controller evaluation. The package preserves campaign-specific directory layouts and historical execution records. A dependency-light deterministic template smoke test supports inspection without language-model downloads or CUDA. Full inference and fitting used NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX 8 GB and platform-specific CUDA/PyTorch environments. Original host paths and observed package inventories are provenance records, not a universal portable lockfile; full main-campaign model weights are referenced by revision and checksum, while the retriever campaign includes its pretrained and clean-fitted checkpoints. A release verifier checks the curated file manifest and metadata. The original retrieval verifier also requires original source paths for its final host-specific integrity checks. Original project software is MIT licensed (SPDX: MIT), with collective copyright held by the MAPE-K contributors. summary: Benchmark data and trained interatomic potentials accompanying Learning nonlocal residuals in interatomic potentials with Fourier neural operators , by Wei Chen and Gian-Marco Rignanese. The files are organized into five benchmarks: homogeneous Yukawa interactions, heterogeneous screening, liquid water, LLZO, and Au2/MgO(001). Each benchmark archive contains its datasets and exact splits, final checkpoints and required local backbones, training recipes, generation or preparation scripts, and evaluation provenance. A shared archive supplies inference code, loading instructions, model indices, and checksums. The collection contains 422 result entries referencing 376 distinct checkpoints: 274 primary entries, 115 appendix entries, ten molecular-dynamics model entries, and 23 diagnostic entries. The heterogeneous benchmark includes the 40-set remote-medium probe. The homogeneous benchmark includes thirty production molecular-dynamics trajectories totaling 12 ns and 24,030 saved frames. Training recipes use YAML for MACE, LES, and FNO, JSON for CACE and CACE-SOG, and the published shell command for the upstream Au2/MgO MACE1 model. Download the shared archive and the desired benchmark archives, then extract them in the same directory. See README.md and the per-benchmark license notices.
title: Benchmark datasets, trained models, and molecular-dynamics trajectories for MACE–FNO

Modeling Vocal-class targets and predictors; B-spline lag basis with a lag-varying ridge; bout-offset target. Manifold selection gates the first feature against a training-fold intercept-only predictor and screens features with an exact sign-flip test over 20 folds ( manifold_n_cv_folds ). Behavioural-response silence controls reject windows touching any vocalization; onset negatives need the same clean history as positives. GLM-HMM: final EM log-likelihood, exact BIC parameter counts, fixed label set across folds. Neural modeling (new package) Kinematic encoding, behaviour control, vocal occurrence / gating / decoding, nested and category decoding, quiet-to-vocal transfer and shift-null inference. Visualizations, GUI, notebooks QLVM overview, map-quality and category figures, property-sweep and torus traversal videos, vocal-pose still and video, bout-decoding figure. Every figure and analysis tunable lives in the settings JSON and is documented; notebooks load imports in cell 1 and settings in cell 2. Code quality ruff clean across src and tests; every test documented; the full suite passes. summary: This record accompanies the two-dimensional supplement to A gauge-invariant measure for lattice chiral fermions by Nathaniel Craig. It contains the supplement and its LaTeX source, together with the curated core reproducibility package, supplied in 65 standard tar.gz core archives and a separate evidence addendum. The supplement studies a two-dimensional chiral SU(5) theory with three conjugate-5 left-handed fermions, one 10 right-handed fermion, and five right-handed singlets. It presents an analytic measure construction on a specified admissible domain and numerical tests of selected currents, gauge responses, and determinant phases. The core archive contains all 74 scientific evidence references cited in the supplement, scientific implementations, the complete free-gap ledger, and the saved inputs needed for three principal scalar replays. It retains reports on other calculations and their limitations, but does not contain every raw matrix or intermediate record for those calculations. Extract all 65 archives into one directory to recover the complete core and run the documented checks. The remainder of the additional-data collection and the superseded full calculation archive are not included. The supported replays check saved evidence and recompute final scalar arithmetic; they do not rerun every historical current integration or matrix calculation. A separate gap replay checks the covering and residual bounds using implementation code shared with the producer. The README, result index, completeness record, manifests, and verification receipts specify the procedures and limits. These two-dimensional checks support, but do not prove, the four-dimensional result. The evidence addendum supplies 123 further scientific files referenced by the reports, including exact error ledgers, control results, fields, plots, and compact input records. Extract it alongside the 65 core archives and follow the updated README. Its verifier checks the added-file hashes and selected exact saved arithmetic for the finite-amplitude two-step curl and direct B1 endpoint comparison. It does not rerun the original matrix calculations or establish the analytic remainder estimate. License scope: Apache-2.0 for project-authored code; CC BY 4.0 for project-generated data and written documentation. Existing third-party licenses and notices remain in force. See LICENSES.txt.
title: Two-dimensional chiral SU(5) measure and calculation records for A gauge-invariant measure for lattice chiral fermions

summary: This dataset is a consolidated, machine-readable record of tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) in Poland from 1998 to 2024, assembled from official publicly-available surveillance products and used as the analytic base for an accompanying surveillance article in preparation for Eurosurveillance. For each of Poland's 16 voivodeships (NUTS-2 administrative regions) and for the country as a whole, the dataset contains: annual notified TBE case counts; quarterly breakdown of cases by onset (Q1–Q4); annual incidence per 100,000 inhabitants; hospitalised case counts and percentages; and annual TBE vaccination registrations, stratified by age (0–19, 20+, total). Case data are drawn from the National Institute of Public Health–National Institute of Hygiene (NIZP-PZH) biweekly bulletin Meldunki epidemiologiczne; vaccination data from the NIZP-PZH annual report Szczepienia ochronne w Polsce; population denominators from the Central Statistical Office of Poland (GUS). Vaccination figures count persons completing the primary three-dose cycle or receiving a booster, not total doses. Released under CC BY 4.0. See README for full column dictionary, scope, and known limitations. An accompanying Python script reproduces the four manuscript figures directly from this dataset. Version 2.0 accompanies the revised manuscript (October 2026): adds the ECDC Atlas extract, administrative boundary file, revision analyses (including negative binomial models with estimated dispersion) and scripts generating Figures 1–5. See CHANGES_v2.0.md.
title: Tick-borne encephalitis in Poland, 1998–2024: master surveillance dataset

The suite is designed as a resource for researchers and practitioners interested in systematically evaluating how well various LLMs perform on digital humanities (DH) tasks involving visual and text-like materials. For detailed test results and model comparisons, visit our results dashboard at https://rise-services.rise.unibas.ch/benchmarks/.

summary: Registered protocol of a systematic review reported according to PRISMA 2020. Question: how much performance do deep-learning models for precision agriculture lose when evaluated outside their training distribution (another farm, season, region, sensor or cultivar) or deployed in real field conditions, and how is deployment evidence (latency, energy, memory, field-trial duration) reported? Status at registration: searches completed on 15-16 October 2026 (Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, OpenAlex, SpringerLink, plus citation searching); 14,174 records after deduplication; title/abstract screening not started. The protocol defines the research questions, search strategy, eligibility criteria (IN.1-IN.6, EX.1-EX.8), dual-reviewer active-learning screening with ASReview LAB and a pre-registered stopping rule (SAFE-based), the data-extraction codebook, the quality-appraisal rubric and the synthesis plan (internal-to-external relative performance loss).
title: Protocol: From benchmark to field: a systematic review of external-validation and deployment evidence for deep learning in precision agriculture
